subject: Request: Everstream APAC latency SLA carveout & temporary service credit cap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@everstream.io>, procurement@everstream.io
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Everstream APAC latency SLA carveout & temporary service credit cap

Hi Tom / Everstream procurement team,

Following our technical sync last week, Everstream has asked us for an APAC-specific latency/availability accommodation tied to the planned edge migration in Singapore. The core ask is: allow a temporary deviation from our standard availability SLO (99.9% global) for APAC-only traffic to a 99.6% target while the new edge fabric is stabilized, with an explicit remediation/credit schedule. They also requested a modest one-time usage credit for the first billing period while the work completes.

Summary of proposed commercial terms to present to Deal Desk and Execs for sign-off:
- APAC SLO: 99.6% availability (APAC region only) for a fixed period
- Duration: proposed 6 months starting upon amendment effective date
- Service credits: sliding scale but capped (proposal below)
- One-time customer credit: 10% of committed usage for month 1 (open to negotiation)
- Monitoring: Redwood to publish an APAC-specific uptime dashboard and share weekly for duration
- Rollback: automatic revert to standard SLO at period end, unless extended by mutual agreement and exec approval

I've attached a draft SLA amendment (SLA-amendment-draft.docx) and Everstream's network topology they provided. Can you confirm whether we have flexibility on the credit cap and duration? If this needs exec approval, please advise who to loop in. I recommend Deal Desk + Sales Exec sign-off because this is an SLO variance + monetary concession.

Next steps I need from you:
- Confirm whether 99.6% / 6 months is acceptable as our starting ask
- If not, provide alternative thresholds you'd accept (e.g., shorter duration or smaller one-time credit)
- Indicate whether Everstream is prepared to sign an amendment via DocuSign (link below)

Thanks — I'll stand by for next steps and can schedule a quick call if useful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA-amendment-draft.docx (draft), everstream-network-topology.pdf (diagram)

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@everstream.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@everstream.io
Date: 2027-02-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Everstream APAC latency SLA carveout & temporary service credit cap

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the draft. We appreciate Redwood being pragmatic here. A few points from our side:

1) Duration — we'd prefer the 6-month window but want an explicit rollback trigger if our traffic normalizes earlier.
2) Credits — we're comfortable with a cap but need it to be no higher than 10% total per month. Anything above that materially damages our internal ROI case.
3) One-time credit — we can accept a one-time credit; 7.5% of month 1 committed spend would be our ask (instead of 10%).
4) Signature — procurement prefers DocuSign for the amendment. We can sign once legal confirms remedy language.

I populated procurement@everstream.io so they can coordinate signatures. Please let us know what you need internally for a decision; if you can get Deal Desk + legal to confirm the credit cap and remedy mechanics, we can move quickly.

Tom
Tom Alvarez
Head of SRE & Cloud Strategy
Everstream Networks

Date: 2027-02-15T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Everstream APAC latency SLA carveout & temporary service credit cap

Marissa — looping in Deal Desk (Ben) and Sales Ops (Vivek) since this is both an SLO variance and a monetary concession. Quick recommendation from a commercial standpoint:

- Cap the total monthly credit at 10% (Everstream asked for this; let's accept).
- Reduce the duration to a 90-day pilot rather than 6 months; gives us a faster rollback and less runway exposure.
- Keep the one-time customer credit at 7.5% (compromise).
- Require a production-runbook and weekly APAC availability report for the duration; if metrics normalize for 4 consecutive weeks we automatically revert.

Ben, can you confirm this is within the allowable deal desk concession band? Vivek, if this needs Exec sign-off, please advise. Marissa, if Everstream is okay with 90 days and 7.5% one-time credit we can expedite the amendment.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-16T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Everstream APAC latency SLA carveout & temporary service credit cap

Quick legal read and redlines — high level items we need before we sign:

1) Remedy mechanics must be precise: define "APAC availability" measurement (which region, which endpoints), measurement interval (monthly), and exact credit formula. Proposed safe formula: 5% credit for each 0.2% below 99.6%, capped at 10% per month.
2) Duration: 90 days is preferable. Any extension should require mutual written agreement and explicit executive sign-off.
3) Limit liability language: no change to total liability other than specified service credits. No other penalties.
4) Force majeure and maintenance windows: ensure standard carveouts apply.

If Sales wants to keep the customer-facing credit language looser, legal will not sign off — we need deterministic terms. I'll attach an annotated amendment today. Vivek — I need an explicit approval for the 90-day term + 10% cap to complete the DocuSign-ready redline.

Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@everstream.io>, procurement@everstream.io
Date: 2027-02-17T15:33:00-07:00
Subject: Approval: Everstream APAC SLO variance (conditional)

Team — after reviewing the facts and Jon's redlines, I approve a conditional executive waiver for Everstream with the following binding conditions:

1) Effective term: 90 days starting on the amendment effective date (no automatic extensions).
2) APAC SLO: 99.6% availability measured at the regional ingress layer described in the legal redline. Measurement interval: calendar month.
3) Service credit schedule: 5% credit for each 0.2% below 99.6%, capped at 10% per month (legal's formula).
4) Customer one-time usage credit: 7.5% applied to the first invoice following amendment effective date.
5) Operational controls: customer agrees to share weekly APAC availability reports; Redwood will publish a public APAC dashboard link. The amendment must include the runbook attachment.
6) DocuSign amendment executed and countersigned by Everstream procurement prior to effective date. No retroactive application.

Ben — proceed with Deal Desk entry under deal ES-4932 and mark this as exec-approved concession. Jonas — please finalize your redline and produce the DocuSign-ready amendment. Marissa — please confirm Everstream is willing to sign the 90-day term and 7.5% credit and send DocuSign link when ready.

Approving on behalf of the Sales leadership team. Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales — Americas
Redwood Inference

--
